docs.title: Response Format
docs.text:
Reference Guide

The Supercard Workforce API uses a standardized JSON response structure across all endpoints. This consistent format simplifies client development, error handling, and response parsing.

Every API response contains predictable top-level fields, allowing applications to process successful and failed requests using a common model.

docs.title: Standard Response Structure
docs.text:
All API responses follow this structure.

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {},
  "meta": {}
}

For failed requests:

{
  "success": false,
  "error": {},
  "meta": {}
}

docs.title: Response Components
docs.text: Field Required Description success Yes Indicates whether the request succeeded. data Success Only Contains the requested resource or operation result. error Error Only Contains error details for failed requests. meta Yes Additional metadata describing the response.

docs.title: Successful Response
docs.text:
Example:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "employeeId": "EMP-1001",
    "employeeName": "Alok Sharma",
    "department": "Engineering"
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "REQ-10101",
    "correlationId": "CORR-7C41A9F3",
    "timestamp": "2025-02-06T15:00:00Z",
    "apiVersion": "v1"
  }
}

docs.title: success
docs.text:
Boolean value indicating whether the request completed successfully.

Example:

"success": true

docs.title: data
docs.text:
Contains the primary response payload.

Depending on the endpoint, this may contain:

  • Employee information
  • Attendance records
  • Leave requests
  • Payroll details
  • Report summaries
  • Export jobs

Example:

"data": {
  "employeeId": "EMP-1001"
}

docs.title: meta
docs.text:
Provides metadata about the request.

Example:

"meta": {
  "requestId": "REQ-10101",
  "correlationId": "CORR-7C41A9F3",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-06T15:00:00Z",
  "apiVersion": "v1"
}

docs.title: Metadata Fields
docs.text: Field Description requestId Unique identifier generated by the API. correlationId Client-generated request identifier. timestamp UTC time when the response was generated. apiVersion API version that processed the request.

docs.title: Error Response
docs.text:
Failed requests return the following structure.

{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "The requested employee could not be found."
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "REQ-10102",
    "correlationId": "CORR-7C41A9F3",
    "timestamp": "2025-02-06T15:10:00Z",
    "apiVersion": "v1"
  }
}

docs.title: Error Object
docs.text: Field Description code Machine-readable error identifier. message Human-readable description of the error. details Optional validation information.

docs.title: Validation Error Example
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
    "message": "One or more validation errors occurred.",
    "details": [
      {
        "field": "email",
        "message": "A valid email address is required."
      }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "REQ-10103",
    "correlationId": "CORR-7C41A9F3",
    "timestamp": "2025-02-06T15:15:00Z",
    "apiVersion": "v1"
  }
}

docs.title: Collection Responses
docs.text:
Endpoints returning multiple resources include a collection inside data.

Example:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "items": [
      {
        "employeeId": "EMP-1001",
        "employeeName": "Alok Sharma"
      },
      {
        "employeeId": "EMP-1002",
        "employeeName": "Priya Shah"
      }
    ],
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "pageSize": 20,
      "totalRecords": 248,
      "totalPages": 13,
      "hasNext": true,
      "hasPrevious": false
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "REQ-10104",
    "correlationId": "CORR-7C41A9F3",
    "timestamp": "2025-02-06T15:20:00Z",
    "apiVersion": "v1"
  }
}

docs.title: Asynchronous Responses
docs.text:
Long-running operations return a job reference.

Example:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "reportJobId": "JOB-20250206-001",
    "status": "Queued",
    "estimatedCompletionTime": "2025-02-06T15:30:00Z"
  },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "REQ-10105",
    "correlationId": "CORR-7C41A9F3",
    "timestamp": "2025-02-06T15:25:00Z",
    "apiVersion": "v1"
  }
}

docs.title: Response Lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR

A[Client Request]

A --> B[API Processing]

B --> C{Success?}

C -->|Yes| D[Return Data]

C -->|No| E[Return Error]

D --> F[Include Meta]

E --> F

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
The response format follows these principles:

  • Predictable structure
  • Consistent naming
  • Machine-readable errors
  • Human-readable messages
  • Standard metadata
  • Forward compatibility

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always inspect the success field.
  • Check the HTTP status code before processing the body.
  • Use error.code for application logic.
  • Log requestId and correlationId.
  • Process data only when success is true.

docs.title: Common Mistakes
docs.text:
❌ Assuming data always exists.

❌ Parsing error messages instead of error.code.

❌ Ignoring the meta object.

❌ Using HTTP status codes alone without checking the response body.

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
Responses never expose:

  • Passwords
  • Access tokens
  • Internal SQL queries
  • Stack traces
  • Database connection details

Only information required by the client is returned.

Use the Meta Object

Store the requestId and correlationId in your application logs. They make troubleshooting significantly easier.

Consistent Across Every Endpoint

Every endpoint in the Supercard Workforce API follows the response structure documented here, providing a predictable integration experience.

Do Not Assume Success

Even when a network request completes successfully, always verify both the HTTP status code and the success field before processing the response.

docs.title: HTTP Status Codes
docs.text:
The Supercard Workforce Management API uses standard HTTP status codes to indicate the outcome of every API request.

Status codes allow client applications to determine whether a request completed successfully or whether additional action is required.

This reference summarizes the HTTP status codes used throughout the API.

docs.title: Status Code Categories
docs.text:
HTTP status codes are grouped into five categories.

Category Range Description Informational 100–199 Request received and processing continues. Successful 200–299 Request completed successfully. Redirection 300–399 Additional action is required. Rarely used by the API. Client Error 400–499 The request is invalid or cannot be processed. Server Error 500–599 The server encountered an unexpected error.

docs.title: 200 OK
docs.text:
The request completed successfully.

Typical examples:

  • Retrieve employees
  • Retrieve departments
  • List attendance records

Example:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK

docs.title: 201 Created
docs.text:
A new resource was created successfully.

Typical examples:

  • Create employee
  • Create department
  • Submit leave request

Example:

HTTP/1.1 201 Created

docs.title: 204 No Content
docs.text:
The request completed successfully, but no response body is returned.

Typical examples:

  • Delete employee
  • Delete department

Example:

HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

docs.title: 400 Bad Request
docs.text:
The request is invalid.

Possible causes:

  • Missing required fields
  • Invalid JSON
  • Invalid parameter values

Recommended action:

  • Review the request payload.
  • Validate all required fields.

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
Authentication failed.

Possible causes:

  • Missing access token
  • Invalid token
  • Expired token

Recommended action:

  • Obtain a new OAuth 2.0 access token.
  • Retry the request.

docs.title: 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
The authenticated user does not have permission to perform the requested operation.

Possible causes:

  • Insufficient privileges
  • Restricted resource

Recommended action:

  • Verify user permissions.

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
The requested resource could not be found.

Possible causes:

  • Invalid resource identifier
  • Incorrect endpoint
  • Deleted resource

Recommended action:

  • Verify the request URL.
  • Confirm the resource exists.

docs.title: 409 Conflict
docs.text:
The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.

Typical examples:

  • Duplicate employee
  • Duplicate department
  • Business rule violation

Recommended action:

  • Resolve the conflict before retrying.

docs.title: 422 Unprocessable Entity
docs.text:
The request is syntactically correct, but business validation failed.

Possible causes:

  • Invalid business rules
  • Invalid field values

Recommended action:

  • Correct the request data.

docs.title: 429 Too Many Requests
docs.text:
The API rate limit has been exceeded.

Recommended action:

  • Respect the Retry-After header.
  • Retry after the specified interval.

docs.title: 500 Internal Server Error
docs.text:
An unexpected server-side error occurred.

Recommended action:

  • Retry the request after a short delay.
  • Record the request ID for troubleshooting.

docs.title: 503 Service Unavailable
docs.text:
The API is temporarily unavailable.

Possible causes:

  • Scheduled maintenance
  • Temporary infrastructure issues

Recommended action:

  • Retry using exponential backoff.

docs.title: Status Code Summary
docs.text: Status Name Meaning 200 OK Request completed successfully 201 Created Resource created successfully 204 No Content Request succeeded without a response body 400 Bad Request Invalid request 401 Unauthorized Authentication required or failed 403 Forbidden Permission denied 404 Not Found Requested resource not found 409 Conflict Business rule conflict 422 Unprocessable Entity Validation failed 429 Too Many Requests Rate limit exceeded 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server failure 503 Service Unavailable Temporary service outage

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
When handling HTTP status codes:

  • Check the status code before processing the response body.
  • Treat all 2xx responses as successful.
  • Handle each 4xx status individually.
  • Retry only temporary failures such as 429 and 503.
  • Log the X-Request-ID for failed requests.
  • Display user-friendly error messages rather than raw API responses.

docs.title: Which status codes indicate success?
docs.text: Any status code in the 2xx range indicates a successful request.

docs.title: Should every 5xx error be retried?
docs.text:
Not immediately.

Implement exponential backoff and limit the number of retry attempts.

docs.title: Why is 404 different from 400?
docs.text:
• 400 Bad Request means the request itself is invalid.
  • 404 Not Found means the request is valid, but the requested resource does not exist.

docs.title: What does 422 mean?
docs.text:
The request is correctly formatted, but one or more business validation rules failed.

Examples include:

  • Invalid salary value
  • Unsupported department
  • Leave dates outside policy

Developer Tip

Build your application around HTTP status codes rather than parsing response messages. Status codes provide a stable and standardized way to determine how your application should respond.

Retry Policy

Do not retry every failed request automatically. Only retry transient failures such as 429 Too Many Requests or 503 Service Unavailable after an appropriate delay.

Portfolio Project

The HTTP status codes described in this document follow standard HTTP semantics and represent the behavior of the sample Supercard Workforce Management API used throughout this portfolio.
